comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
🚨 **BLOCKING: false "resolved NOTHING from the secure store — those providers boot keyless" warning on the documented project/user-config queue flow**

`referencedSecureKeyNames` now folds in `queueEntryKeyNames(queueEntries)` for project/user-scope queues (bin passes `queueResolution.entries` whenever `scope != ProviderQueueScope.env`). But the "resolved NOTHING" warning in `secureKeyBootDiagnostics` is purely store-based: it fires when **none** of the referenced names resolve **from the store**, regardless of whether the key resolves from the environment. For a queue, `apiKeyEnv` pointing at an env var is the *canonical* key shape — `buildProviderQueueChain` itself says "keys never ride in the queue blob; name the env var holding the key", and the shipped skill doc (`prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md`, "Provider queue" section) documents exactly this setup:

```yaml
providersQueue:
  - provider_type: openai-completions
    provider_config:
      model: moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6
      baseUrl: https://gate.example/v1
      apiKeyEnv: OPENAI_API_KEY
```

Reproduced against this branch (probe over the exact boot sequence in `queue_only_headless_boot_test.dart`, secure store empty, key present in env):

```
warning: 1 provider key(s) referenced by the config (custom providers /
roles) resolved NOTHING from the secure store — those providers boot
keyless; re-enter a key or run with --debug-secrets ...
```

The provider does **not** boot keyless (the env key resolves and the queue serves), so every boot of this flow now prints a false alarm with wrong remediation ("re-enter a key"). The env-scope queue is excluded for precisely this reason ("env-only setups reference nothing — the boot warning must stay silent for them"); a project/user-config queue with env-sourced keys is the same key-source situation and should stay silent too.

Suggested fix: filter `queueEntryKeyNames` by env presence before joining the diagnostics set (same rule `freshInstallProviderState` applies — a name with a non-empty env value is not store-referenced), e.g. in `bin/fah_runapp.dart` pass `queueEntries: <entries whose key names are unset in env>` when `scope != env`, or add the env filter inside `queueEntryKeyNames`'s caller. The preload set (`secureKeyPreloadNames`) can keep the unfiltered names — preloading a name the env shadows is harmless.

Please also add the missing IT: a project-scope queue (`providersQueue:` in `<tmp>/.fah/config.yaml`) with an env-only `apiKeyEnv` must assert `bootDiagnostics` is empty — the current E3 test only covers the env scope, which is why this slipped through.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the boot-time rebuild loses the rotation stack — boot and rebuilt queues disagree on multi-credential entries**

`collectQueueSecrets` now sweeps the rotation stack (`NAME_2`, `NAME_3`, …) from the environment so multi-credential entries build real `ApiKeyRing`s. That only works on the **boot** path, where the real `Platform.environment` reaches the sweep. The post-boot rebuild path cannot see it:

- `attachProviderQueueQuotaFeed` runs on **every** queue boot and calls `_rebuildProviderQueueRuntime(warn: false)`;
- `_rebuildProviderQueueRuntime` builds its env view via `_queueSecrets`, which constructs a map containing **only the base names** (`apiKeyEnv`, `refreshTokenEnv`, the chatgpt default slot) — no `MY_KEY_2`/`MY_KEY_3` entries;
- `collectQueueSecrets`'s new stack sweep iterates exactly that map, so it finds nothing → the rebuilt `config.providersQueueRuntime` carries **single-key rings** where the boot build had the full stack.

Result after this PR: on every queue boot the config-level runtime (what `/providers queue list`, the queue editor health rows, `_providerQueueTest` probes and `_providersQueueStatusLabel` read) silently diverges from the runtime the constructor actually wired into the agent — and any future code that re-binds `config.providersQueueRuntime` into the live agent would silently drop keys 2..n. The rebuild is also the path a `/providers queue add/remove/move` edit takes (loud `warn: true`), so an edited multi-credential queue degrades the same way.

Suggested fix: make `_queueSecrets` sweep the stacks from the real environment — e.g. seed the map it hands to `collectQueueSecrets` with `NAME_\d+` entries from `Platform.environment` (or pass the process env as a fallback source), so boot and rebuild resolve identical secret snapshots. A regression test mirroring `UT-queue-secrets-rotation-stack` through `AgentCli.attachProviderQueueQuotaFeed` would pin it.

(Context: the rebuilt runtime is currently only read by the queue UI/probe surfaces — the constructor binds the boot runtime's `streamFunction` and nothing re-reads the config field into the agent. That pre-existing #823 wiring gap is not this PR's regression, but it is why the divergence is observable rather than harmful today.)

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: the entry→key-name ladder now exists three times — share `queueEntryKeyNames`**

This PR introduces `queueEntryKeyNames` as the single helper for "which key names does a queue entry reference", but the same ladder (`?apiKeyEnv`, `?refreshTokenEnv`, chatgpt default slot when `apiKeyEnv == null`) is still duplicated inline in two places that must stay in lockstep with it:

- `collectQueueSecrets` (lib/src/cli/startup.dart:1200 — the `names` list built inside the loop)
- `AgentCli._queueSecrets` (lib/src/cli/agent_cli_commands.dart:979 — the env-map keys)

If a fourth key slot ever joins the ladder (say a third credential kind), three of the four sites must be edited in sync. Suggest rewriting both inline lists as `queueEntryKeyNames([entry])` (or iterating it), keeping this PR's new helper the one source of truth.

```dart

    'rendered — no second print',
```

The PR otherwise formats cleanly (the incidental `secureKeySaveDegradationLines` re-indent in startup.dart suggests a formatter pass ran over lib/ but missed this test file).

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: document the `queueResolved` contract in `startupApiKey`'s dartdoc**

`startupApiKey`'s prose doc explains `baseUrl`, custom entries and `[pinnedKeyName]`, but the new `queueResolved` parameter — which changes the gate's contract from "missing key = hard startup failure" to "optional lookup, the queue owns the stream" — is only explained by the inline comment at the assignment. Since this flips the fail-loudly behavior the headless boot relies on, a sentence in the dartdoc (and `[queueResolved]` in the param prose) would help the next reader who lands on this signature without the gh-1781 context.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: One blocking correctness bug: project/user-config queues with env-sourced `apiKeyEnv` keys (the documented canonical shape) now print a false "resolved NOTHING from the secure store — those providers boot keyless" warning on every boot (reproduced on this branch). Plus one important issue (the post-boot queue rebuild loses `NAME_2`/`NAME_3` rotation stacks) and three suggestions.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `referencedSecureKeyNames` + `secureKeyBootDiagnostics`: config-scope queue keys are store-probed but never env-checked → false "boot keyless" alarm on the documented flow (`prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md` queue example)
- ⚠️ `_queueSecrets` builds a base-names-only env map, so `collectQueueSecrets`'s new rotation-stack sweep never fires on the quota-feed rebind / queue edits — rebuilt runtime silently drops to single-key rings
- 💡 Entry→key-name ladder duplicated 3×; one test file not `dart format`-clean; `queueResolved` undocumented in `startupApiKey` dartdoc

**Next Steps**:
1. Filter env-resolved names out of the diagnostics set (keep them in the preload set) and add the missing project-scope IT
2. Seed `_queueSecrets` with rotation-stack names from the process env; pin with a rebind-level rotation test
3. Share `queueEntryKeyNames` across the three sites; run `dart format`; document `queueResolved`

Note (outside this diff, pre-existing): `fa serve --a2a` / `--bridge` and wire-serve runners stream the legacy model+key lane and never consult the queue runtime — with a queue-only boot they serve an empty key; worth a follow-up.
